findings.fix_hint: resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosOrdersTrackerComponent.vue — bind a chip {{order.delivery_boy_name}} when order.delivery_boy_id is truthy; trigger a 2-second toast after a successful assignment mutation.

findings.evidence: State 01 network log contains a 422 on GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/admin/fiscal/z-report (the only network entry in the file). This is logged WITHOUT any [role=alert] / .toast / .alert visible in the DOM (verified). 422 on a GET to z-report on the suivi-commandes page suggests the tracker is firing an out-of-context fiscal report query that always 422s — a silent error wired to the daily cash close UI. If admin had a real reason to view z-report and it 422s silently, NF525 close visibility is broken. Not on the allowlist (logout 401, form 422, csp 204, 304 cache).
findings.fix_proposal: Inspect resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosOrdersTrackerComponent.vue (or the Suivi mount layer) for a guard-free `apiCall('/api/admin/fiscal/z-report')`. The endpoint controller likely requires a date param the tracker isn't passing. Either (a) stop calling it from the tracker, or (b) pass {date: today} and surface 4xx via UI toast.
findings.fix_hint: grep -r 'fiscal/z-report' resources/js → find the call site; either guard with `if (route.name === 'admin.fiscal.z-report')` or pass required `date` query param. Backend: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/Fiscal/ZReportController.php — check rules in the FormRequest.

findings.evidence: Detail-page state 02 + state 07 render the customer name as 'Wave T E2E 177930039..' (two dots, not Unicode ellipsis U+2026) in the 'Informations De Livraison' card. findings.fix_hint: Find the show-order template — likely resources/js/components/admin/pos-order/PosOrderShowComponent.vue or admin/pos-order/show.blade.php — and remove the hard JS substring(0, 22) + '..' pattern; replace with CSS `.delivery-customer-name { max-width: 260px; text-overflow: ellipsis; }` and bind `title="${name}"`.

findings.evidence:
State 02 detail-page DOM contains literal 'N° commande: #Wave' rendered. The order's `token` value is 'Wave' (4 chars — the 'Wave T E2E ...' customer name truncated upstream as a token at the first space) and the UI prints it as if it were the order code. Full DOM context: '
  • N° commande: #Wave

Either the field is meaningless and should be removed for non-online-platform orders, or the token storage needs proper validation. In state 07 (DELIVERED) the same garbage '#Wave' remains.
findings.fix_proposal: Hide the 'N° commande: #<token>' row when the order is not an external-platform order (Deliveroo/UberEats/etc.), OR validate that token has reasonable length/format before storing. The token field is documented for delivery aggregator integration; using it for POS-typed customer names produces this garbage.

The seeder/spec at tests/e2e/__fixtures__/wave-t-orders.json (or the controller that wrote token) is also a vector — but display-side guard is the V1 fix.

findings.evidence: All four `db_state_*` snapshots in the capture report show `total_amount: 0` for order id=70 (verified: db_state_initial.total_amount=0, db_state_after_assign.total_amount=0, db_state_after_out_for_delivery.total_amount=0, db_state_after_delivered.total_amount=0). But every UI surface and the API response body sample show `total: 19` and `total_currency_price: '19.00€'`. The `orders.total_amount` column is therefore not the source of truth for the displayed total — the UI must be computing total from items each render, leaving the persisted column stale at 0. Risk: reports that read directly from `orders.total_amount` (NF525 z-report aggregations, daily cash close, sales-by-category) will under-report revenue by 100%. NF525 chain integrity is byte-identical for this branch, but the upstream business-revenue read path is broken.
findings.fix_proposal: Either (a) backfill `orders.total_amount` at order creation in the storeOrder pipeline (immediate fix, schema unchanged) OR (b) document `total_amount` as deprecated and audit every consumer to use the computed total. (a) is the V1 path: in app/Http/Controllers/Admin/PosOrderController.php or the relevant order-create service, set `$order->total_amount = $computedTotal` before save.
findings.fix_hint: grep -r 'total_amount' app/Models/Order.php app/Services/Pricing/PricingService.php app/Http/Controllers/Admin/Pos*Controller.php. Likely the column is filled only for non-POS order types and skipped for POS DELIVERY orders. Sentinel: PHPUnit test asserting `Order::find(X)->total_amount > 0` after any order with subtotal > 0.

findings.evidence: Spec admits explicitly (lines 50-60): 'Why API path (not UI assign dropdown) : ... The delivery-boy assignment UI in PosOrderShowComponent depends on a modal that varies by route version (v4 vs v5). Driving by API tests the canonical contract.' Result: the delivery-boy dropdown CLICK PATH (the only flow a real cashier uses) is NOT exercised by this E2E. The 200 on POST /select-delivery-boy proves the controller works; it does NOT prove (a) the dropdown loads available drivers, (b) only branch_id=1 drivers are listed (multi-tenant isolation), (c) the option click correctly fires the assignment, (d) the modal closes and the parent refreshes. State 02 DOM does show a dropdown widget rendered with 'Livreur Test Wave T' as a li — but the spec never clicks it. GStack PASS attestation 'driver assigned id=13' is technically true but UX path untested.
findings.fix_proposal: Add a second spec wave or a follow-up Wave D-bis that drives the UI dropdown click instead of the API: page.click('.dropdown-btn:has-text("Sélectionner un livreur")'); page.click('text=Livreur Test Wave T'); then assert the same 200 + UI feedback. Keep the API path as a complementary contract-level check.
findings.fix_hint: Add page.click sequence in a new test() block or in the same spec under flag UI_DRIVER_FLOW=1. The dropdown selector pattern: `.dropdown-group > .dropdown-btn` (data-v-ad6d7c16 from the captured DOM). The li selector after open: `.dropdown-list > li.active`.

findings.evidence: `db_state_after_pretransition` (snapshot taken right after the PREPARING→PREPARED transition, target_status=8 per API extra) shows `status: 13` (DELIVERED). Right after, `db_state_after_assign` shows status=8 (PREPARED). This is logically impossible if both snapshots come from sequential reads — DELIVERED is a terminal state in OrderStateMachine, an order shouldn't roll back from 13 to 8. Either (a) the spec re-used order #70 across runs and the snapshot timing is off (race between idempotent pretransition write and DB read), or (b) the state machine permits illegal backward transitions. Risk: if (b), then a malicious or buggy client could downgrade a DELIVERED order to PREPARED, then to OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, etc., breaking fiscal reporting.
findings.fix_proposal: Add an explicit sentinel test: `OrderStateMachine::transition(DELIVERED, PREPARED)` MUST throw / return false. Re-run Wave D from a fresh fixture (no order #70 reuse) and verify the snapshot ordering shows monotonic forward transitions only.
findings.fix_hint: tests/Feature/Order/OrderStateMachineMonotonicityTest.php — assert no backward transitions from DELIVERED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, RETURNED. If the spec is reusing order #70, the fixture file should be re-generated per Wave A run (timestamp suffix already does this for the customer name, but the order id should also be new each run).

findings.evidence: State 05 PNG shows the LIVRÉS column with both Wave A's order #1 (TAKEAWAY 'Client passage', 17,00 €) AND Wave D's order #2 (LIVRAISON 'Wave T E2E 1779300395176', 19,00 €) in the same lane with identical visual styling (pos-tracker-card--muted class for both). There is no visual differentiator between a TAKEAWAY-delivered order and a DELIVERY-completed order in the final lane. A driver returning later wouldn't know which orders they themselves handled. Compare: state 01 shows the 'tag' (1×) icon next to a basket icon but no order-type pictogram.
findings.fix_proposal: Add a small order-type icon (truck for LIVRAISON, bag for À EMPORTER, ticket for CAISSE) to each tracker card title row. The data is available — order.order_type is 5 (DELIVERY) for #2 and a different enum value for #1.
findings.fix_hint: PosOrdersTrackerComponent.vue card template — next to `N°A0002` add `` with a small helper that maps OrderType enum to icon class.

findings.evidence: The 'Sélectionner un livreur' control on the detail page (state 02 DOM) is implemented as a custom <div class='dropdown-group'><button class='dropdown-btn'>... a <ul class='dropdown-list'> of <li> items. It is NOT a native <select> element — no native keyboard nav (Tab+Down arrows), no aria-haspopup, no role='listbox', no role='option' on the <li>. The <li> has no tabindex. Screen-reader users will hear the button label ('Sélectionner un livreur') but cannot expand the list via keyboard or hear that 'Livreur Test Wave T' is an option. Same widget reused for status dropdown ('Payé', 'Préparée', 'En Préparation', etc.) — multiplies the issue 3× on the detail page.
findings.fix_proposal: Wrap the dropdown with proper ARIA: button → aria-haspopup='listbox' aria-expanded={open}; <ul> → role='listbox' aria-label='Sélectionner un livreur'; each <li> → role='option' aria-selected={x===current} tabindex='0' with keyboard handlers (Enter, Space, Arrow keys).
findings.fix_hint: The dropdown component is registered as `data-v-ad6d7c16` — likely a shared `<DropdownGroup>` in resources/js/components/ui or admin/shared. Patch once, propagates everywhere. Sentinel: a Playwright check that `getByRole('listbox')` resolves on the detail page.

findings.evidence: Detail-page DOM contains 'BIG CAYENNE - Salade, Tomate, Oignon' and 'SANDWICH CAYENNE - Salade, Tomate, Oignon' rendered as INSTRUCTIONS for the order items. These are duplicated item labels in ALL-CAPS without translation, but they appear in a section labeled 'Instruction:' — suggesting the instruction field is being auto-populated with the item name+composition rather than driver-facing notes. A real cashier writing 'Pas de sauce, allergie' would see their actual instruction replaced or appended-to by this auto-text. Minor in V1 LOCAL (only Cayenne menu) but a label/data semantics bug.
findings.fix_proposal: Audit the order_items.instruction column usage — is it auto-populated for display, or are real user instructions overridden by item-name template? If display-only, rename the label from 'Instruction:' to 'Composition:' to disambiguate.
findings.fix_hint: grep -r 'instruction' resources/js/components/admin/pos-order/show* — find binding. Possibly resources/views/admin/pos-orders/show.blade.php. Either rename label or split into two fields.

findings.evidence: On the detail page state 02 + state 07, the 'Frais De Livraison' row in the right-side totals card shows the value '0.00€' in green text on white background. The green is a positive/success color (~#1a7f37) on white — passes for plain text but the value is '0.00€' which is NOT a positive event (no delivery fee free-shipping celebration intended). Visually misleading. Also: green-on-white at small body-text size with that hex tests around 4.0:1 contrast — under AA 4.5:1 floor.
findings.fix_proposal: Use the default body-text color (~#212529) for the 'Frais De Livraison' value when delivery_charge === 0, and only green when delivery_charge > 0 AND there's a discount/free-delivery promo applied. Better yet, remove the row entirely if value is 0.
findings.fix_hint: Detail page totals card template. The 'green' class is likely a hard-coded class on the delivery-charge <span>. Conditional binding: `:class="order.delivery_charge > 0 ? 'text-success' : 'text-body'"`.

findings.evidence: Capture report observations include 'api token extracted from vuex localStorage : true' AND 'api_key_used: b6d68vy2-m7g5-20r0-5275-h103w73453q120'. The 'api_key_used' string is NOT a valid hex UUID — it contains non-hex chars (m, g, r, h, w, q). Either (a) a placeholder logged instead of the real token (safe — the real token came from Vuex), or (b) the spec is dispatching API calls with an opaque non-standard token format. If (b), the auth path in production may accept arbitrary string formats (low risk: Sanctum tokens are 40-char hex, so this would 401, but we see all 4 API calls returned 200 — meaning the real token came from Vuex and this string is a misleading log line).
findings.fix_proposal: Update the spec to log the actual token used (first 8 chars + '...' for safety) instead of a placeholder, OR remove the misleading 'api_key_used' field from the capture report so reviewers don't waste time investigating a non-token.
findings.fix_hint: tests/e2e/test-e2e-wave-t-caisse-to-delivered-D-livreur.spec.js — find where capture.api_key_used is set and either remove the line or set it to `token.slice(0,8) + '…'`.

notes: Adversarial review of Wave T Round 1 Wave D LIVREUR. GStack PASS attestation is technically correct on the contract layer (4 API calls 200, NF525 chain appended 13→14, branch isolation respected, DB state monotonically advances 8→10→13) but the UX layer is broken: (a) State 04 OUT_FOR_DELIVERY status has NO tracker lane → order vanishes from cashier view between 'Livré' click and 'Delivered' final, P0 silent disappearance; (b) State 03 driver-assigned has NO UI feedback on the tracker card → cashier may re-click thinking the assignment failed; (c) state 01 fires a silent 422 on /api/admin/fiscal/z-report with no toast → silent_error P0. The cashier-flow assertion in GStack PASS ('driver assigned via UI') is misleading — the spec admits it bypasses the dropdown via direct API call (WT-D-R1-09 P1 audit_integrity). Numeric integrity issue: orders.total_amount column persists 0 while UI computes 19,00€ from items (WT-D-R1-08 P1) — z-report aggregations that read total_amount will under-report revenue. Recommendation: RED verdict, block delivery to owner until WT-D-R1-01 (EN LIVRAISON lane), WT-D-R1-05 (z-report 422), and WT-D-R1-08 (total_amount=0) are healed. Frozen-zone discipline respected (no writes to NF525-critical fiscal services). Owner-mandate principle 'no return with broken state' → RED.
